brand.name: Tubro Construction
brand.palette_guidance: Lock the real logo green #0C883D and near-black #231F20. Favor bright warm whites, restrained construction neutrals, and authentic wood/stone tones from client project photography. No invented cyan identity, washed-out gradients, stock indigo, or dominant orange discount styling.
brand.voice: Professional, warm, plainspoken, confident, and respectful of the homeowner’s investment.
brand.identity_belief: A remodel earns trust when homeowners can see the work, understand the path, and know who is accountable from estimate through completion.
brand.visual_metaphor: A continuous measured construction line travels through the page like a chalk line or plan mark, joining finished spaces, project stages, and the next clear decision.
taglines: Built Around the Way You Want to Live

hard_rules: Use the real Tubro Construction logo asset as-is. Never redraw, restyle, re-letter, or reinterpret the logo; frames may use a neutral placeholder or plain wordmark only.
Use authentic supplied Tubro project photography before all generated or stock imagery. Never generate imagery that impersonates a completed client project.
No van-led hero. A branded vehicle may appear only as secondary brand context and is not required in these homepage refs.
No dark, boxy, heavy-card redesign; no generic centered service-card grid; no pill-heavy SaaS UI; no gradient text or generic gradient blobs.
No generic stock families, contractor portraits, invented team members, or generated named people.
No invented testimonials, ratings, awards, licenses, bonding, insurance, warranties, project counts, project locations, budgets, or timelines.
Keep the site clearly separate from Tubro Carpet Cleaning and Get Gawn; do not mention those businesses in customer-facing homepage copy.
Keep the 5% active-duty military and first-responder discount secondary to the free-estimate CTA. Do not add a deadline, urgency claim, or new terms.
Do not imply direct Buildertrend integration; form leads route to workorders@tubroconstruction.com and office staff enter leads manually.
Use location names naturally. No repetitive city-name stuffing or doorway-page language.
Every visual control must have a useful defined outcome. Otherwise render it as static content.
Design for desktop and mobile accessibility with strong contrast, clear labels, and visible focus intent.
Customer review and approval are required before public launch.
Frames cover CONTENT sections only; global nav/footer belong to the built design system and are never rendered into frames.
source_constraints: Manifest text wins for build copy.
Do not invent location-specific projects, team claims, ratings, licenses, timelines, project counts, addresses, or testimonials.
Use authentic supplied Tubro photography only as project/capability evidence described in this manifest.
